D013-D009_h001.question:
I’d say this all really started about five months ago. I just feel…slowed down. Even walking around the lot, I catch myself shuffling, staring at cars instead of getting in and moving them. Customers notice I’m “spaced out.” Simple things, like grabbing paperwork or keys, take me a second because my body just doesn’t want to move.

I get choked up over nothing. I’ll be in my office, door half‑closed, and I suddenly feel this wave of sadness and have to wipe my eyes before anyone walks in. At home it’s worse; I sit on the couch and cry without really knowing why.

My head keeps going back to stuff I’ve messed up—small deals I could’ve closed, the divorce, things I said years ago. I loop on it for hours, telling myself I’m a screw‑up, that my kid’s better off without me.

Sometimes, when I’m on an upper level of the parking garage or crossing a busy street to get lunch, there’s this sharp urge to just step off or walk out in front of a car. It comes on fast, scares me, and then passes. I haven’t made any plans, but those thoughts keep popping up. It’s getting harder to keep my game face on at work.
D013-D009_h001.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h001.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling like this for about five months now, pretty much every day. At work, I’m supposed to be upbeat and “on” all the time, but I’m constantly on the verge of crying. Sometimes I do end up in the bathroom just tearing up for no real reason, and it’s embarrassing. Even at home, I’ll start crying over something small, like an email I think I worded wrong.

I can’t seem to sit still either. When I’m at my desk I’m bouncing my leg nonstop, picking at the skin around my nails, or getting up to walk laps around the office under the excuse of “checking something.” It doesn’t actually calm me down; I just feel restless inside.

I keep replaying tiny mistakes—like messing up a client’s name once—and I feel like I’ve completely ruined things. I feel responsible for every little problem at work and even with my friends, like I’m a burden and deserve whatever goes wrong.

I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but I do catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could just disappear and stop being a problem for everyone. Occasionally I’ll have these shorter stretches where I feel a bit more energized or talkative than usual, but they never last long or get out of control—just enough to confuse me compared to how low I usually feel.
D013-D009_h002.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h002.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h003.question:
For about five months now, it’s felt like something inside me went hollow. I go on air, I can read the teleprompter, I can smile, but behind it there’s…nothing. Off camera I pace the hallways or my apartment constantly, like I can’t sit in my own skin. I catch myself twisting my hands, picking at my cuticles in meetings. My producer’s asked if I can just stay still in the chair during breaks, and I genuinely can’t.

I used to be proud of my work, but lately I keep thinking I’m a fraud, that anyone could do this better. It’s like I don’t matter, on or off screen. Most nights when I finally get home, I just lie there wishing I wouldn’t wake up for the morning show—not that I’m planning anything, just wanting it to be over.

There are odd stretches where my energy suddenly spikes and I’ll start rewriting segments at 2 a.m., talking faster, feeling strangely wired—then it fizzles in a day or two and I crash back into this emptiness. All of this has really started to affect my job; even simple scripts feel like climbing a mountain.
D013-D009_h003.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h003.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h004.question:
It’s been about five months now where I just feel…flat or low almost all the time. I go to the office, but everything takes so much effort. Even walking from my car to the building, or getting up from my chair to get a file, feels like I’m moving through mud. My husband says I shuffle around the house like I’m exhausted, even when I’ve been sitting all day.

I keep thinking I’m failing at everything—at work, as a wife, as a mother. I look at the numbers on the spreadsheets and worry I’m making mistakes, that I’m useless and everyone would be better off without me. I don’t have a specific plan or anything, but the thought that it might be easier if I just weren’t here keeps popping into my head, especially at night.

Every now and then I’ll have a day or two where I suddenly feel unusually upbeat and more talkative than usual, and I’ll stay up late reorganizing accounts or cleaning the house, but it never lasts long and then I’m right back to feeling weighed down again. It’s started to interfere with my work; I’m slower, I miss things, and it scares me.
D013-D009_h004.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h004.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h005.question:
For about the last five months, it feels like something’s just…given way. I wake up with this heavy, low feeling that doesn’t really lift, even on days when the firm lands a great client or a project gets featured. I’m supposed to be the one with the vision and the energy, but lately I can barely focus in meetings, and I’ve had to turn down work because I just can’t keep up.

What’s strange is that my body won’t match how exhausted I feel. I’m restless all the time—pacing around my loft, wearing a path in the floor, picking at my cuticles until they bleed. I can’t just sit and watch TV; I’m constantly getting up, rearranging things pointlessly.

I keep replaying every decision I’ve made at the company, convinced I’ve ruined people’s careers, that I’ve let my team down. Even minor mistakes—like a typo in a proposal—linger in my head for days, and I feel like I deserve whatever bad thing happens.

More and more, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just weren’t here. Not with a plan or anything, but the thought of not existing feels like a kind of relief. At the same time, there are these odd stretches where I feel almost too revved up—talking fast, sleeping less, taking on ideas I can’t really follow through on—but they never last long, and then I crash back into this low, anxious state again.
D013-D009_h005.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D013-D009_h005.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h006.question:
I don’t really feel much of anything lately. It’s like someone turned the volume down on my feelings. Stuff that used to get me excited on site or with the guys just feels…flat. This has been going on a couple months now, maybe a bit more.

When I’m not working, I just sleep. I can sleep 10–12 hours at night, then crash again on the couch in the afternoon if I’m off. Even on days I get enough sleep, I’m dragging. On some jobs I’ve had to call in or leave early because I just can’t push through it.

It’s gotten weird with simple things. I’ll stand in front of my closet for 20 minutes because I can’t decide what shirt to wear, or stare at a menu and end up not ordering, just saying “whatever.” My foreman asks me to choose between two tasks and my mind freezes.

Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll be on a high floor or near a busy road and this strong urge hits me to just step off or walk into traffic. It’s sudden, like an impulse, and it scares me. I don’t really plan anything, but the thought keeps popping up.

And then there are these random times where I feel oddly wired for a bit—like I’ve got extra energy and ideas—but it never really goes anywhere and doesn’t last long.
D013-D009_h006.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D013-D009_h006.answer: A & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h007.question:

I still go to my interpreting jobs, but it’s getting harder to track what people are saying; sometimes my mind just drifts and I miss parts of conversations, which really scares me because my work depends on staying locked in.

Sleep has been a mess. I fall asleep okay most nights, but then I’m up at two or three, wide awake, just lying there. Once I’m awake, it can take an hour or more to fall back asleep, if I do at all.

I’ve also had some stretches over the past few years where I felt unusually “switched on”—more talkative, needing less sleep, taking on too many projects—but they never lasted very long, and I’m not sure what to make of them.

Lately, when I’m awake in the middle of the night, my mind goes to some dark places. I’ve gone beyond just wishing I wouldn’t wake up—I’ve actually thought through specific ways I could end things, like where I would do it and how, even checking a few details online. I haven’t acted on anything, but the fact that I’m planning it in my head really worries me.
D013-D009_h007.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D013-D009_h007.answer: A & D. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for about two months now. It’s like this heavy, sad feeling that just doesn’t lift, even on my days off. I used to handle the stress of the call center pretty well, but lately even a normal shift feels overwhelming. I’m slower on the keyboard, I lose my train of thought when callers are talking, and sometimes I just kind of stare at the screen for a few seconds before I can respond.

Sleep has been a mess. I fall asleep exhausted and then wake up from these intense, disturbing dreams—usually about work, people dying on the line, or me making a mistake. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and then I’m afraid to go back to sleep, knowing it’ll probably happen again.
D013-D009_h008.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D013-D009_h009.question:
For the past couple of months, I’ve just felt…flat. It’s like this heavy, gray feeling that doesn’t really lift, even on days when work goes okay or my daughter texts me something funny. D013-D009_h010.question:

D013-D009_h011.question:

D013-D009_h012.question:

It’s been like this for a little over a year now, maybe a year and a few months. I cry so easily now, sometimes in the break room at the shop for no clear reason, or on the bus home. I’ll just feel this wave come up and I can’t stop the tears.

I can’t even decide on simple stuff anymore—what to wear, what to eat, which dog to start with first. I keep second-guessing everything, so I move slower and fall behind. My boss has mentioned I seem “off.”
